sentences.text:
Gopinath Kar vs The State Of West Bengal & Ors on 30 January,
2026
S/L 44
30.01.2026

Gopinath Kar
 Vs.
 The State of West Bengal & Ors.
 Mr. Kumar Jyoti Tewari, Sr. Adv.
 Mr. Amrit Sinha
 Mr. Aniruddha Tewari

Mr. Ansar Mandal
 Mr. Wasim Ahmed
 Mr. Mshehabuddin

Ms. Somshree Dey
 ... for the State.

Mr. Swapan Banerjee
 Mr. Diptendu Narayan Banerjee
 ... for the respondent no. 5.

1. Learned advocate appearing for the State submits that the original Case Diary is misplaced and
they are having the second copy of the Case Diary and if this Court will pass an order, the police will
reconstruct Case Diary.
2.  It is found from the record that on completion of investigation, the police has submitted charge-sheet for the offence under Sections 498A/304B/34 IPC.

As the matter is triable by the Sessions Court, accordingly, the case has been transferred to the learned Court of Sessions Judge and it has been registered as Sessions Case No. 8(1) of 2012, Sessions Trial Case No. 1(5) of 2013 with computerized S.C. No. 171 of 2014.
3. This Court intends to know whether all the original documents collected by the investigating officer during the investigation has submitted the same along with the charge-sheet before the Court.

Accordingly, the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Fast Tract Court No. 2, Barasat, North 24 Parganas is directed to submit a report before this Court, whether the charge-sheet submitted by the police on the basis of which the charge has been framed against the accused persons contains all the original documents i.e., a) FIR, b) seizure memos, c) documents, d) charge-sheet and other documents which the prosecution has relied upon as per the list of documents mentioned in the charge-sheet.

5. List this matter on February 18, 2026.
6.
The petitioner as well as the department is directed to communicate this order to the leaned Additional Sessions Judge for compliance.
7. Report filed by the State be kept with the record.

(Krishna Rao, J.)
